title: Evaluation of the tabulated circuit
statement: Let $\kappa$ be a finite set of instruction kinds, let $m,w,n$ be nonnegative integers, let $F$ assign to each kind a function from Boolean lists to Boolean lists, and let $z$ be a Boolean list. Consider a finite program whose instructions each have a kind and an ordered list of source bits; suppose every source in instruction $i$ is valid when the available input bits are $z$ followed by $n$ input bits and the output width is $w$, and every instruction has exactly $m$ sources. For any input assignment $x:\mathrm{Fin}\,n\to\mathrm{Bool}$, program position $o$ within the program, and output coordinate $j<w$, the tabulated circuit's value is the $j$th bit of the block produced by instruction $o$ when the program is run on the concatenation of $z$ and $x$, with missing list entries interpreted as false.
